thread:
Alex Carter: Quick evening handoff — I’m leaving the bridge in Priya’s hands. Summary first: we saw a spike in routed 503s starting ~21:12 UTC affecting hosted inference (mostly short chat routes). Paging and mitigations already in flight. Details below, chronological.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered 21:12 UTC — alert: routed-503-rate > 5% (prod-hosted). Alert ID: pager-9876. Auto-notifications sent to #eng-oncall and primary.

Alex Carter: Root cause hypothesis at the moment = cascade of cold-KV misses after a cache invalidation + sudden traffic burst causing busy GPUs -> some requests timed out at the routing layer. KV miss rate jumped and batching backpressure made a subset of worker pods return 503s.

Mateo Ruiz: Observed logs from router: `upstream error: all workers busy` and `503: request timed out while waiting for worker`. Miss-rate metrics: `kv_cache.miss_rate` 12x baseline at 21:13.

Lin Chen: I pushed a temporary routing rule at 21:18 to divert non-SLA traffic to the cheaper fallback pool. Command: `POST /routing/override { "route": "non-critical", "target": "fallback-small" }` — verified in routing logs.

Priya Shah: I’ve accepted primary for next 12h. Mateo is next up as secondary. Lin is infra on-call for node scaling and health. Sam will coordinate customer comms if we need external messages.

Samir Patel: I have a draft status note ready in #customers (internal) — will wait for final confirmation on impact windows before posting publicly. Current impact: degraded latency and some 503s for a subset of user requests; not a full outage. Approx ~4% of requests saw 5xxs during the peak minute.

Alex Carter: Mitigations applied so far:
- scaled dedicated worker pool `redwood-dedicated-prod` 6 -> 12 (manual scale via deployment)
- enabled routing fallback to `gpt-small-quant` for non-critical endpoints
- warmed prefix cache for top 20 prefixes via one-off job `cache-warm-2026-06-14`
- temporarily relaxed sequence-length batching to reduce kv-cache pressure

Mateo Ruiz: Commands and outputs I ran (copied):
```
$ kubectl scale deployment redwood-dedicated-prod --replicas=12 -n inference
deployment.apps/redwood-dedicated-prod scaled
$ kubectl get hpa -n inference redwood-worker
NAME              REFERENCE                     TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
redwood-worker    Deployment/redwood-worker     120%/80%  6         24        12
```

Lin Chen: Notable log snippets around 21:13:
```
[21:13:17] warn: kv-cache: miss-rate spike 78% (prefill=0) -> cold-start cascade
[21:13:24] error: router: dispatch timeout -> 503
[21:14:02] info: autoscaler: spawning extra pods (requested by manual scale)
```

Priya Shah: Current status (21:45 UTC):
- routing 5xx rate down to ~0.6% (from peak ~4.2%)
- latency still mildly elevated for some tail requests (~200ms extra p95)
- fallback routing active for 14 routes (non-critical)
- dedicated pool at 12 replicas, autoscaler re-evaluating thresholds

Alex Carter: Outstanding action items before handoff complete:
1) Priya: keep primary until 07:00 PT (confirm overlap if you need extension).
2) Mateo: capture heap and KV cache profiles from 21:10–21:20 window and upload to /internal/share/incident-1865432100/profiles.
3) Lin: add a temporary HPA floor bump to avoid repeated cold starts overnight; propose min pods=8 for next 24h.
4) Samir: hold off public customer note until we confirm scope with telemetry team; internal update in #customers (draft ready).
5) Alex: file INF ticket and assign to infra + runtime teams for postmortem and runbook updates.

Mateo Ruiz: I’ll handle the profiles and attach them to the ticket. Also setting up a short eval to quantify quality difference between `gpt-small-quant` and main model for fallback traffic.

Priya Shah: Noted on coverage: we have an APAC coverage gap 02:00–06:00 UTC where no SRE is scheduled; recommend asking for on-call overlap tomorrow morning or enable more aggressive autoscaler policy for that window.

Lin Chen: I’ll open a config PR to set HPA min=8 and bump evaluation window to 60s. Attaching PR link once ready.

incident-bot: incident-1865432100 created and linked. Severity: Sev2. Current state: mitigation. Pager log: 21:12 triggered, 21:18 reroute engaged, 21:25 manual scale complete.

Alex Carter: Handing off — Priya primary, Mateo secondary, Lin infra, Sam customer comms. My last note: if you see a repeat spike, revert fallback and scale faster (use `./scripts/scale-fast.sh`) to avoid prolonged cold cascades — we've got an automation gap here.

Priya Shah: Taking it. Will monitor dashboards and check-in at 22:15 UTC. If anything changes I’ll ping the team and reopen the bridge. :thumbsup:

Samir Patel: Copy — will prep comms and stand by.

Mateo Ruiz: All done on profiling; files uploaded and linked in ticket INF-1865432100.

Lin Chen: PR for HPA min bump: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/432 — tagging @PriyaShah for approval.

Alex Carter: Follow-ups for postmortem:
- owner: Mateo Ruiz
- timeline and root cause writeup (KV prefix invalidation + traffic spike)
- runbook updates: add a section on `cold-start cascade` mitigation, include `scale-fast.sh` and fallback routing checklist
- cost/ops impact and recommended SLA adjustments for low-priority routes

Priya Shah: Acknowledged. I’ll triage overnight if noise returns. Leaving Slack notification on for immediate pages.

Alex Carter: Thanks all — handoff complete.

--- End of thread ---
